subject: science
prompt:
# Same Atoms, Different Answer

Take a pebble and take your own hand. Weigh out what they are made of and you get the same short list: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, a few others.

> **So where does the difference come from?**

Commit to an answer before we go looking. You will not be marked on it.

options.text: Living things contain kinds of atoms that non-living things do not.
options.feedback: It is a fair guess, but the list really is the same. Nothing on it is exclusive to life.

options.text: Living things contain far more atoms than non-living things.
options.feedback: A boulder beats you comfortably on atom count, and it is not alive.

options.text: The difference is in how the atoms are arranged and what that arrangement does.
There is an extra ingredient in living things that has not been discovered yet.
options.feedback: People believed this for a long time. Every place it was looked for, it was not there.
